title: Dynamic short issue IDs: default 4-character hash prefix, widened only on collision
description:
Change how Kanbus abbreviates an issue's hash prefix for display (CLI and console). Short IDs currently show 6 characters (for example kbs-60bf38).

New design: a dynamic prefix length.
- By default, show 4 characters of the hash in short IDs (for example kbs-60bf). The default is configurable via `short_id_length` in .kanbus.yml; Beads compatibility mode implies 6 unless explicitly set.
- Collision checks are project-wide, not just within the visible list: a displayed short ID is unique among the live issues sharing its project key (shared + local together). Within a rendered set, only colliding groups widen, iteratively, with no cap on width.
- The full original ID is always kept. This changes only how much of the ID is shown in a given context, never the stored ID.
- Unique-prefix lookups (kbs show <prefix>, --parent <prefix>, and so on) keep working via hyphen-insensitive matching, and existing longer references in comments, commits and docs still resolve. When a prefix matches multiple issues, the disambiguation picker (task kbs-26d651) presents the candidates; non-interactive callers get a structured error with full IDs and a stable exit code, and retry once with a full ID.
- Stored text (wiki pages, story-directory paths, commit messages, summaries, agent provenance commands, newly written references) uses full IDs; display-only contexts use the formatter. `kbs validate` flags stored references that have become ambiguous.

Why:
- 4 characters saves tokens for agents and cuts visual noise for people reading the UI.
- Collisions at 4 characters are uncommon per pair but expected at board scale; the extra characters are paid only where they occur, and the picker makes the rare ambiguity recoverable instead of fatal.
- Full IDs in stored text keep long-lived references stable.

Out of scope: GitHub's commit-hash display.

comments.text:
# Dynamic short ID design review — consolidated decisions and requirements

Folded in from the gap review of this epic. These are decisions, not open questions. Where a file is named, it is a call site that the epic's checklist must cover.

## 1. Complete formatter site inventory (the "everywhere" list was incomplete)

The centralized formatter replaces every remaining truncation site, not just `ids.rs`, `ids.py`, and the two console matchers:

- Comment-ID prefixes in ambiguous-comment errors: `rust/src/issue_comment.rs:92`, `python/src/kanbus/issue_comment.py:89`, `rust/src/beads_write.rs:204` — route through the formatter (dynamic, default 4).
- Comment IDs shown by `kbs show`: `rust/src/issue_display.rs:249`, `python/src/kanbus/issue_display.py:260` — same dynamic treatment within the show output.
- Inline hand-slicing in sync output: `python/src/kanbus/jira_sync.py:128` and `snyk_sync.py:228,576,612` (`kanbus_id[:find("-")+7]`) bypasses `format_issue_key` entirely — route through the formatter; the printed column width becomes the max formatted width of the batch instead of the fixed `:<14`.
- Provenance-warning command (`rust/src/agent_metadata.rs:260`, `python/src/kanbus/agent_metadata.py:301`): it emits a copy-paste `kbs comment update …` command, i.e. stored text — per the stability policy below it embeds the **full ID**, not the formatter.
- `packages/ui/src/kanban/format-issue-id.ts`: a third front-end formatter (used by `TaskDetailPanel.tsx` and `StatusTree.tsx`) that hard-codes 6 chars and **uppercases** the project key. Delete it; the shared TS formatter from kbs-c118a7 covers `packages/ui`, and the uppercase-key behavior goes away (lowercase everywhere).
- Doc comment `rust/src/issue_creation.rs:246` ("up to 6 chars") is updated with the implementation.

## 2. Matcher correctness

Hyphen-insensitive prefix comparison everywhere IDs are matched: `issue_identifier_matches` (rust/src/ids.rs), `matches_issue_identifier` (python/src/kanbus/ids.py), `short_id_matches` (rust/src/console_backend.rs:291), `shortIdMatches` (apps/console/src/App.tsx:424). Removing the `> 6` cap alone is not enough in the console matchers — they compare against the hyphenated UUID suffix, so 9+ character display IDs would never match. Dotted sub-IDs are compared as base + suffix separately.

## 3. Collision universe (which issues count)

- Group by project key, not by directory: shared + local + same-key virtual-project issues form one collision namespace (`console_backend.rs` merges shared and local under one key). The resolver's candidate universe must equal the formatter's universe, otherwise a displayed short ID could silently resolve to a different issue.
- Tombstoned issues are excluded from width computation (they cannot be displayed). A stale prefix that matches a tombstone plus a live issue goes to the disambiguation picker, not a silent pick.
- Beads compatibility mode keeps the beads 6-char scheme: `beads_compatibility: true` implies `short_id_length: 6` unless explicitly configured; widening on collision still applies (display-only; beads storage is untouched).
- Keyless (project-context) display is only valid in single-project output. Any multi-project output includes project keys, so keyless cross-project collisions cannot occur.

## 4. Stability policy for stored text

Full IDs in anything stored or long-lived: wiki templates/pages (`issue.id`, including story-directory link paths currently built from `issue.key` per CONTRIBUTING_AGENT.md:392), commit messages, right-now summaries, agent provenance-warning commands, and newly written dependency/parent references. Existing short references keep resolving via prefix match. `kbs validate` gains a check that flags stored references (deps, parents) that currently match more than one live issue.

## 5. Performance

Collision scans read file names only (`list_issue_identifiers`-style listing across shared + local dirs) — never parse issue JSON bodies. The wiki render cache is already invalidated by any issue change (`wiki.rs:1015` hashes all ids + updated_at), so no extra work there. The daemon index cache and console snapshots invalidate on issue-file changes as they do today; the console derives display widths client-side per snapshot and never caches widths beyond snapshot lifetime.

## 6. Configuration

`short_id_length` (default 4) in ProjectConfiguration (`rust/src/models.rs`, `python/src/kanbus/models.py`, `python/src/kanbus/config.py` defaults), documented in CONFIGURATION.md, and included in `ConsoleSnapshot.config` so the console TS formatter reads the same value. `beads_compatibility: true` implies 6 unless explicitly set.

## 7. Rust / Python / TypeScript parity

One Gherkin spec executed by both harnesses covers the formatter, the matcher, and the ambiguity error shape. A checked-in JSON fixtures file is shared by Rust, Python, and TS tests so all three implementations are verified against identical inputs. Monkeypatch hazard: Python tests patch `cli.format_issue_key` in roughly ten test files (`test_cli_issue_commands.py`, `test_cli_bulk_delete_list.py`, `test_issue_display_line.py`, …); the refactor must update those patches to the new list-formatter entry point, or the tests keep passing while no longer exercising the real path. Make the patch audit an explicit checklist item.

## 8. Testing

Replace the exact 6-char fixtures (`features/issues/issue_key_representation.feature`, `python/tests/test_ids_text_editor_templates.py`, `id_format_steps.rs/py`, `issue_key_steps.rs/py`) with property tests: injectivity (the formatted set is unique), minimality (no ID is longer than necessary), determinism, and width stability. Collision fixtures: a 4-char collision pair; local-vs-shared same-key pair; two projects sharing a key; dotted sub-IDs; widening past 8 chars (the hyphen case); beads IDs; numeric-only IDs; unicode custom IDs (JS slices UTF-16 code units while Rust/Python count code points).

## 9. Agent token tradeoff (documented in CONTRIBUTING_AGENT.md)

The 4-char default saves about two characters per displayed ID, but one ambiguity round-trip (error + retry) costs more than that saves across a whole list. Guidance for agents: use `--json` (full IDs) for scripted work with many ID operations; on ambiguity (exit code 3), retry once with the full ID from the structured error; never guess longer prefixes.
